findings_to_judge.finding: Yext's own pillar metric went sequentially negative: ARR from customers >=$50K fell from $403.6m at 31 Jan 2026 to $403.1m at 30 Apr 2026 and its YoY growth halved from +2% to +1%, while that cohort's net retention rate dropped 99% -> 97% and total company NRR dropped 97% -> 95% in a single quarter. Straight-line extrapolation puts the >=$50K cohort - 91% of all ARR and the single line management points to as proof of a turn - at zero-to-negative YoY growth in the quarter being reported on 1 Sep.

Sell-side revenue estimates have not been cut at all after last quarter's miss: Zacks consensus for Q1 FY27 was ~$111.5m (actual $107.92m, a 3.21% miss) and the consensus now carried into Q2 FY27 is $111.30m - essentially the identical dollar figure - even though the ARR base entering Q2 ($440.8m) is $3.5m lower than the base entering Q1 ($444.3m). The only thing bridging the gap is the extra three days in the May-Jul quarter.

The entire ~50% quarterly rally happened on zero company information: Yext's last substantive press release was 17 Jun 2026 and it made no SEC filing of any kind after 13 Jul 2026 (the 18 Aug release was only the earnings-date notice). Over that newsless window short interest rose to 5.59m shares / 6.67% of a 83.8m float with 4.63 days to cover, RSI reached 75, and the stock passed both published price targets ($5.00 Finviz, $6.67 MarketBeat) and the $5.75 price at which the company itself bought 24.3m shares in March.

Yext has permanently removed the mechanism behind its only two positive earnings reactions. The Q4 FY26 letter states 'We will no longer provide forward-looking financial guidance' and 'We are suspending quarterly earnings conference calls'; the 18 Aug earnings-date release mentions no call or webcast. Both of the up-prints in the baseline's eight-event history were beat-and-raise / M&A-news events (2025-06-03 +31.5%, 2025-08-18 +8.8%) - a guidance raise is now impossible and there is no Q&A in which management can reframe a weak metric.

A company that says it gives no guidance did quietly set a hard numerical bar for this exact quarter, buried in the 2 Jun shareholder letter: 'GAAP Net Income margins in the 10-15% range in Q2, Q3 and Q4' and 'Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion towards 30%'. Q1 FY27 GAAP net income was only ~2.2% of revenue ($0.02 basic EPS on $107.9m), so hitting the low end of its own range in Q2 requires GAAP net income of roughly $11-17m - a 4-7x sequential jump - against a rising interest bill on $150m of newly drawn term debt.

The offsetting positive tail: $114.9m of repurchase authorization was live for the whole of Q2 FY27 with ZERO open-market buybacks used as of 30 Apr 2026 ($14.9m remaining plus $100.0m added by the board in May 2026, disclosed as a subsequent event), while the stock traded between the $3.27 52-week low and ~$5.75 for most of May-July. Two directors bought personally in the same window - Seth Waugh 133,000 shares at $3.746 on 11 Jun and Daniel Englander 76,190 shares at $5.2226 on 13 Jul - and the CEO had bid $9.00/share for the company in 2025. The 1 Sep 10-Q is the first disclosure of whether the company bought, and shares outstanding were still 100,248,116 as of 19 May.
